verdict.label: Worth checking
verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Lunch
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY, I’d check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam before I leave, because Rey Cortiço at lunch is the best available option but the wind angle isn’t great and the Surfline consistency has been a bit weak. The tide’s around dead low and it can still line up on the sandbanks, but it sounds like a “rare window” kind of day. Only head out if the cams look noticeably cleaner than expected; otherwise I’d skip it.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Medium confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 25 kJ, 9 s period, lully 1/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
